newsitem.title: UK: LME grinds to a halt in PM, markets close steady.
newsitem.headline: LME grinds to a halt in PM, markets close steady.

text.p: Base metal markets failed to excite during Tuesday afternoon LME trading, as earlier advances petered out, and by the end of the kerb prices were broadly steady.

Traders said volumes and liquidity were low-key for most of the day - a trend that has prevailed for some time and is likely to continue. Consequently, there were some price movements that were amplified by the thinness of the conditions.
"Take copper, it goes up $10 at a time, but the volume is just dribs and drabs. There are low volumes and low enthusiasm at the moment," one said.
Copper did push up to $2,380 at one stage, against the background of the strike at Chile's Quebrada Blanca mine, but there was little followthrough, and the inevitable downturn followed.
"It did not manage to hold it, and then just drifted back this afternoon," the trader said.

By the close, three months was back at an unchanged $2,360 a tonne, and seemingly set to remain a $2,320/2,380 jobbing market for the short-term. The cash/threes backwardation was little changed at $65/70.
Elsewhere, price rallies in aluminium and zinc similarly fizzled out, although both markets remained in the plus column.
Aluminium business was restricted to a tight range, but last trade was at $1,632 a tonne, up $8 from the close of last Friday.
Zinc prices remained firmer, although the market eased back from the highs near $1,290 to finish at $1,277, up $15.
Traders said the slippage from the highs reflected profit-taking once the short-covereing rally seen in the morning faded.
Nickel prices continued to trade in a narrow band, but edged up during the afternoon to close at $7,470, a $40 gain from pre-weekend levels.
Lead conditions were slow throughout, and the modest $3 advance to a closing $626 reflected the general trend.
Tin busuiness was also fairly slow, but the market held onto initial gains. Last trade was at $5,800, up $60.
Alloy did not move from the $1,500 level, with three months ending at $1,500/1,505 a tonne.
